answer-xl.purpose: The band's answer on an empty day. Fluid; breaks to two lines on a 375px phone and fills the green field.

answer-lg.purpose: The band's answer on a one-event day.

answer-sm.purpose: The band's answer from two events up, where the cards are the answer and the band steps back to one line.

document-title.purpose: The /terms page heading. The only display size outside the band.

title.purpose: Event card titles and the band's next-event when-line.

title-compact.purpose: A Coming up row's title — one density step below a card title.

numeral.purpose: The day of the month in a Coming up date stamp. Tabular.

lede.purpose: The next event's title inside the green band.

control.purpose: Form fields, bordered buttons, loading text, /terms body.

body.purpose: Event descriptions, form labels, the submit ask. Column caps at 660px, about 70 characters.

meta.purpose: Venue, footer, field errors, the stale note. Also the card's leading time line at weight 700 in the accent.

meta-sm.purpose: Band top line, source hostname, Share, Read more, character counter, Coming up meta.

label.purpose: Region names: 'Coming up' and the band's kicker. Uppercase, tracked 0.11em.

label-sm.purpose: Tag stamps, week strip day letters and counts, the Coming up date stamp.

shadows.name: attention
shadows.purpose: A card or Coming up row under the cursor, on hover-capable devices only. No translate — a card is not clickable.

shadows.name: stuck
shadows.purpose: The week strip once it reaches the top of the viewport. The system's one authored motion moment.

shadows.name: rest
shadows.purpose: The base layer of the deep-link pulse keyframe. Not used as a resting shadow on any surface.

shadows.name: sheet
shadows.purpose: The modal sheet, which floats over the scrim rather than over the page — the sole untinted shadow.

shadows.name: focus-halo
shadows.purpose: A focused form field, paired with an accent border.

shadows.name: focus-halo-invalid
shadows.purpose: An aria-invalid field, paired with a Validation Red border.

shadows.name: deep-link-pulse
shadows.purpose: The mid-keyframe of the two-beat pulse on a card arrived at by deep link.

motion.name: duration-quick
motion.purpose: Shadow, colour and underline-colour transitions on cards, buttons and text actions.

motion.name: duration-standard
motion.purpose: The strip's stuck shadow, modal opacity and scale, form field border and halo.

motion.name: card-stagger
motion.value: cardFadeIn 0.3s ease-out both, 40ms per card, capped at 440ms from the 12th card on
motion.purpose: The list's entrance. The cap is what stops a long Saturday from crawling in.

motion.name: skeleton-pulse
motion.purpose: The loading placeholder. The system's only looping animation, and the one that matters most under prefers-reduced-motion.

motion.name: deep-link-pulse
motion.purpose: Two beats on a card reached by a shared link, then still.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.value: @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) — animation:none on .event-card, .skeleton-line, .deep-link-highlight; transition:none on every named interactive control
motion.purpose: Honoured control by control, by name. A new transition must be added to that list in the same commit.

narrative.overview:
The page is a light room with one saturated object in it. A green field runs the full width at the top and says, in words, whether anything is on today; below it a seven-column strip of numbers shows the week ahead; below that a single column of square white cards is the evidence. Nothing else in the interface is loud. There is no webfont, no serif, no monospace, no icon set, no photography, no category palette and no rounded corner on the page itself — the system UI stack with tabular figures carries display, body and every numeral.

The green is a field, not an accent. It owns a whole region rather than dusting a neutral page with brand colour, and at 5.62:1 against white both display and body type clear WCAG AA on it, which is the technical fact that let the band carry the day's answer at all. Everywhere else the accent appears it is small and functional: a time, a link, a tag stamp, a focus ring.

Density is tight and vertical. The primary device is a phone belonging to someone who may be older than the median web user, so every control clears 44px and every affordance carries a real word rather than a glyph. Confirmed rejections: purple gradients and SaaS hero patterns, Facebook Events clutter, aspirational photography, the generic multi-column aggregator grid.
keyCharacteristics: One saturated field, one accent hue, one tag stamp.
Square everything on the page; radius exists only in the modal layer.
Hairlines, not shadows, define surfaces at rest.
System stack only; tabular figures where numbers align in a column.
44px touch floor everywhere, as a product constraint.

rules.name: The One Field Rule
rules.body: The accent appears at full saturation in exactly one full-width region per screen — the band. A second saturated green block anywhere below it makes the ask compete with the answer; everything under the band gets the accent as type, hairline or ring, never as a slab.

rules.name: The Red-Is-Validation Rule
rules.body: danger and danger-tint are reserved for form validation. Nothing informational, no 'stale data' note and no empty state is allowed to borrow them — an empty day is the page's most common state, not an error.

rules.name: The Pressable Line Rule
rules.body: If an element's border is its affordance, that border is border-interactive and must measure 3:1 against every ground it can sit on. border is a whisper; a control cannot afford one.

rules.name: The Tabular Figures Rule
rules.body: Every figure on this site is a time, a date or a count, and all three are read down a column. font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums is set on the band's next-event line, the week strip counts, the card's time line and the Coming up date and meta. Any new numeral read in a column inherits it.

rules.name: The Sentence, Not The Stamp Rule
rules.body: Body-level content is set in sentence case. Uppercase with tracking is reserved for the three label steps, which name a region ('Week ahead', 'Coming up') or stamp a category ('Free', 'For kids'). A venue, a title or a description is never tracked uppercase.

rules.name: The Answer Outranks The Name Rule
rules.body: The brand line sets at 0.75rem beside the date; the day's answer sets between 1.25rem and 2.75rem. On a page whose whole job is one question, the largest thing is the reply, never the wordmark.

rules.name: The Sized-By-Its-Answer Rule
rules.body: The band is one component in one order, sized by its own content and never by its own importance: is-xl when nothing is on (the answer fills the field and hands over the next real event), is-lg at one event, is-sm from two up, where the cards are the answer and the band gets out of their way in a single line. This is the system's signature move; anything new that occupies the band obeys it.

rules.name: The Seven Days Rule
rules.body: The week strip is the entire date navigation: seven fixed days from today, and no further. Fixed columns cannot reflow under a thumb the way the previous four-button row did. Anything beyond the seventh day is the footer's date picker, kept deliberately out of the way because going more than a week out is the rare visit.

rules.name: The 44px Floor Rule
rules.body: Every interactive element clears a 44px minimum dimension — by min-height on text actions, by padding where a border would otherwise draw at the wrong place, by sizing the wrapping label around a native checkbox. This is a product constraint from an audience that skews older, not a style choice, and it is not negotiable against density. Adjacent targets may touch; they may never overlap.

rules.name: The Dash, Not The Zero Rule
rules.body: A day with nothing on prints an en dash in Nil Grey at weight 400, not a 0. A column of numerals containing zeroes reads as data; a dash reads as 'nothing', which is the answer.

rules.name: The Flat-At-Rest Rule
rules.body: No surface carries a shadow at rest. A shadow means the user is doing something — hovering, focusing, scrolling a header into place, or opening a sheet. Page shadows are tinted with the ink hue, never pure black; the modal sheet, which falls on the scrim rather than the page, is the sole exception.

rules.name: The Motion Budget Rule
rules.body: One authored motion moment (the strip's shadow as it sticks), one staggered entrance (cards fade in over 0.3s at 40ms steps, capped at 440ms so a long list never crawls), one looping animation (the skeleton pulse), and one two-beat pulse for a deep-linked card. Everything else is a 0.15–0.2s transition on colour, border or shadow. prefers-reduced-motion is honoured control by control, by name, for every animation and transition in the system — adding a new one means adding it to that list.

rules.name: The Squares Rule
rules.body: New surfaces on the page get 0 radius. If a new element wants a corner, it belongs in the modal layer or it is a native form control; there is no third case.

rules.name: The Three Treatments Rule
rules.body: A link's treatment states what it is, and the three are not interchangeable: a neutral Pressable Line underline is a destination whose text gives no other clue that it is one (the venue name); no underline with accent text is an outbound link whose text already announces itself (the source hostname); a pale green 2px underline at 4px offset is an in-page action (Share, the submit ask), thickening to full accent on hover. This was arrived at by fixing a real regression. Do not collapse the three.

rules.name: The Text-Action Rule
rules.body: A secondary action on a listing is text, not a box. A bordered 44px button with a radius was the heaviest object on a card whose whole language is hairlines, six times over on a Saturday. The 44px floor is held by padding instead.

rules.name: The Venue Is A Name Rule
rules.body: A card names a place, not an address: location.split(',')[0], in sentence case, with the full string on href and title. width: fit-content keeps the 44px floor while stopping the target from covering the empty half of the row.

dos: Do define every surface on the page with the 1px hairline (border). It is the system's structural element; shadow and spacing do not replace it.
Do draw every pressable edge in Pressable Line (border-interactive) and measure any replacement at 3:1 against card white and the page ground.
Do size the band by its own answer, never by its own importance.
Do keep the events list one column wide at every breakpoint.
Do set font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums on any figure read down a column.
Do give every interactive control a 44px minimum touch dimension and a real text label — an unlabelled glyph is never the only affordance.
Do carry the accent below the band as type, hairline or ring only.
Do point accent-color at the accent on any native radio or checkbox.
Do tint page shadows with rgba(20,23,26,…); the modal sheet, which falls on the scrim, is the sole exception.
Do add any new animation or transition to the prefers-reduced-motion block by name in the same commit.
Do keep the day's count honest about the day, not about whatever is filtered or rendered beneath it.
donts: Don't put a border-radius on anything that sits on the page. Radius belongs to the modal layer and native form controls, and nowhere else.
Don't add a webfont. There is none, and the three-dependency budget now extends to fonts.
Don't reintroduce a serif or a monospace face. Tabular figures do the mono's old job.
Don't add a second saturated green region below the band.
Don't bring back a per-category colour palette. One tag stamp, one voice.
Don't use danger or danger-tint for anything but form validation — an empty day is the most-shown screen, not an error.
Don't translate a card on hover. Rising toward the cursor claims the whole card is clickable; it is not.
Don't let two 44px targets overlap. Touching is fine; overlapping means a tap on one lands on the other.
Don't set body-level content in tracked uppercase.
Don't extend the week strip past seven days, or reintroduce a stepping date control that reflows under the thumb.
